prompt:
Hand-cut layered paper art, handcrafted stop-motion paper diorama aesthetic.

Create ONE character or object sprite, rendered entirely as handcrafted paper art: a figure assembled from individually cut pieces of matte colored cardstock and fine-grain craft paper.

STYLE:
Strongly emphasize the physical nature of real paper: visible paper fibers, subtle cardstock grain, crisp cut edges, slightly imperfect hand-cut contours, and tiny natural variations in shape. Use simple, graphic silhouettes and charming handcrafted forms rather than realistic modeling. Each object should be simplified into a small number of flat paper shapes, generally using only one or two solid tones per element. Avoid excessive internal detail.

Create depth primarily through PAPER LAYERING, not through realistic light-and-shadow modeling. Individual paper pieces should sit slightly above or behind neighboring layers, creating narrow, soft, clearly separated cast shadows along their cut edges, like stacked cardstock mounted with tiny spacers. Keep all shapes internally flat and evenly colored. No volumetric shading inside leaves, bean pods, soil, stones, or plants.

CRITICAL STYLE RULE:
Flat paper shapes must remain visibly FLAT.
Do not create volume by shading the interior of a shape.
A leaf, bean pod, cloud, stone, or plant must look like a flat silhouette cut from cardstock, not a miniature three-dimensional object.
Depth may appear ONLY through overlapping separate sheets and the thin cast shadow underneath their cut edges.

Use occasional very shallow debossed or embossed paper details for simple veins, folds, grooves, or decorative lines, but keep these extremely subtle. They should look pressed into paper rather than sculpted.

SUBJECT AND POSE:
The little mermaid: a young mermaid girl with long wavy straw-gold (#D9A94E) paper hair falling past her shoulders, pale cream skin, rosy paper cheeks, a quiet thoughtful kind face with a small gentle smile. She wears a plain white hanji-paper vest (a simple sleeveless cream-white paper top with a small round neckline; NO shell bra, NO bikini, NO bare midriff). Below the waist she has a mermaid tail built from 3 big flat overlapping pale-teal (#7FBFB5) paper scale plates stacked like roof tiles plus ONE flat fan-shaped tail-fin piece in a slightly deeper teal (#4F9A90) at the end; the tail is clearly flat cut paper with no glossy scales and no gradient. Simple friendly picture-book character with a big round head (2.5-head body proportion: the head is large, the body short). Floating upright in the water, side view facing LEFT, the tail curving gently down and back in a soft S shape, both arms relaxed slightly away from the body, hair drifting a little, gentle smile, eyes open. Full figure from the top of the head to the tip of the tail fin.

FACE (characters only): a simple cut-paper face — two round dot eyes, a tiny dot nose, a small curved paper-strip mouth, two round pale-pink paper cheeks. No realistic eyes, no eyelashes, no glossy highlights. Objects that are not characters have NO face.

If a reference image is attached, it shows how this character (or this family of objects) is drawn in this exact style: keep the same drawing style, body shapes, face and proportions; take the COLOURS, clothes, markings and POSE from the SUBJECT text above when it says so.

FRAMING:
Square 1:1 image. The whole figure is visible and centred, filling about 80% of the frame. Background: a completely flat, uniform, solid magenta (#FF00FF) chroma-key sheet with no texture, no floor, no ground shadow, no extra props, no border. Nothing else in the image.

LIGHTING:
Use soft, diffuse studio-style lighting from the upper-left, mainly to reveal the edges and spacing of stacked paper layers.
Shadows should be short, soft, restrained, and consistent.
They must feel like paper-layer shadows, NOT realistic sunlight shadows cast by natural three-dimensional objects.

OVERALL FEELING:
Warm, tactile, whimsical, handcrafted, elegant, slightly imperfect, sophisticated paper craft, photographed straight from the front. All cast shadows fall toward the LOWER RIGHT (light source at the upper left), short and identical in direction on every piece.

NO text.
NO photorealism.
NO glossy surfaces.
NO realistic 3D modeling.
NO inflated or rounded forms.
NO clay-like volume.
NO gradients.
NO painterly rendering.
NO airbrushed shading.
NO realistic sunlight shadows.
NO deep ambient occlusion.
NO thick beveled edges.
NO plastic appearance.
NO felt or fabric appearance.
NO fur-fibre texture.
NO magenta or hot-pink anywhere inside the subject.
